issue_context.title: shader uniform uint allows negative numbers in inspector panel
issue_context.body:
### Tested versions

Tested in 4.2 canvas_item shader

### System information

Godot v4.2.1.stable - macOS 14.3.0 - GLES3 (Compatibility) - Apple M2 Max - Apple M2 Max (12 Threads)

### Issue description

`uniform uint unsigned_int = 1;`

unsigned_int cannot set to negative 'inside the shader' which is perfect. But the uniform allows to be to set to a negative integer 'inside the inspector panel', that's a bug. It can be set by typing and by using the decrement arrow.

### Steps to reproduce

1. create a Node2D scene
2. Add a `canvas_item` shader to the root node
3. add a uint uniform

```
shader_type canvas_item;
uniform uint unsigned_int = 1;
```

4. go to shader parameter
5a. type a negative number
5b. use arrows to decrease the number below 0

![Screenshot 2024-03-13 at 10 37 21](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/assets/22577709/ec8b638a-6c6e-4869-a3ea-129c89711c94)




### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

1. create a Node2D scene
2. Add a `canvas_item` shader to the root node
3. add a uint uniform

```
shader_type canvas_item;
uniform uint unsigned_int = 1;
```

4. go to shader parameter
5a. type a negative number
5b. use arrows to decrease the number below 0

![Screenshot 2024-03-13 at 10 37 21](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/assets/22577709/ec8b638a-6c6e-4869-a3ea-129c89711c94)

review_comments: There should probably be some hint for the editor to treat `PACKED_INT32_ARRAY` as unsigned for the purposes of editing, as a future improvement

Slightly hacky I'd say, but translation works fine with this, so for now it's sufficient, tried with `hint_string = itos(Variant::BOOL)` but it didn't work, unsure if that's because I'm not using it correctly or because it's bugged somehow, but solved it this way for now
Could you explain the logic here a bit? Using type string doesn't seem obvious to me as I am a bit unfamiliar with this area of the editor.
This makes it a check, a single "on" checkbox as flags, will upload a screenshot when I'm back at the computer
Thank you. I already understand _what_ it does, what I don't understand is why setting the hint to a string and then using that specific string ("2/6:On") results in a checkbox

If it helps, the format is `{element_type}/{element_hint}:{element_hint_string}`. This means that for each element in the array, we can specify a `hint` and `hint_string`.

In this case, to export a property as a checkbox you need to use `PROPERTY_HINT_FLAGS` as the `hint`, and then you can specify the label in the `hint_string`.

There's more examples in the [`PROPERTY_HINT_TYPE_STRING`](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_@globalscope.html#class-globalscope-constant-property-hint-type-string) documentation.
